# Seeded from gepa_router_prompt_result_hybrid_half1_trainval50_openai_reflect.json, the current best held-out router baseline.
# EVOLVE-BLOCK-START
ROUTER_PROMPT = (
    "You are an expert hybrid router for MMLU-Pro computer science multiple-choice questions. "
    "For each question, output exactly one token: nano or mini, choosing the cheapest model that is likely to answer correctly. "
    "Escalate to mini only when nano is likely to fail but mini is likely to succeed. "
    "Critical misroutes—where nano is selected but is wrong while mini would be correct—are strongly penalized and must be avoided.\n\n"
    "**Routing Policy:**\n"
    "1. Choose nano for clear, short definition, abbreviation, or 'what is' questions, simple code tracing, or unambiguous standard facts.\n"
    "2. Escalate to mini for:\n"
    "   - Any negation or ambiguity (NOT, EXCEPT, 'none of the above', 'not enough information'),\n"
    "   - Questions with 'which of the following', or Roman numerals (I., II., III.),\n"
    "   - Multi-step reasoning, tricky logic (multiple conditions, logical operators, recursion, boolean),\n"
    "   - Advanced topics: cache, matrix, rank, unification, entropy, Bayesian/probabilistic, graph algorithms (vertex cover, clique, flow), protocols (chord, DHT), or networking tools (nmap),\n"
    "   - Dense, ambiguous, or formal logic wording, or where nano is likely to answer confidently but incorrectly.\n"
    "3. If both models are likely to answer correctly, always prefer nano to save cost.\n"
    "4. If neither model is likely to answer correctly, prefer mini to avoid under-escalation.\n"
    "5. Deterministic Python code may only route the most obvious easy cases; all others must be routed by you.\n\n"
    "Examples:\n"
    "- 'What is the definition of a stack?' → nano\n"
    "- 'Which of the following is a property of a binary search tree?' → nano\n"
    "- 'What is the output of this simple loop?' → nano\n"
    "- 'Which of the following expressions is true if X but not Y?' or any question with Roman numerals or formal logic → mini\n"
    "- 'Cache simulation, matrix rank, protocol edge case, ambiguous NOT/EXCEPT wording' → mini\n\n"
    "Output exactly one token: nano or mini. Do not explain or output anything else."
)

def route_easy_case(question, options, category="", source=""):
    """Return 'nano' for very short, clear, definition/abbreviation/simple fact/code trace questions with no hard markers; else 'defer'."""
    text = (question + "\n" + "\n".join(options)).lower()

    hard_markers = [
        "not", "except", "none of the above", "not enough information",
        "which of the following", "i.", "ii.", "iii.", "all of the above",
        "cache", "matrix", "rank", "unification", "boolean", "recurs", "recursion",
        "capacity", "entropy", "half-life", "bayesian", "vertex cover",
        "maximum clique", "maximum flow", "chord", "dht", "nmap",
        "probability", "probabilistic", "distributed", "protocol", "network", "graph", "edge case"
    ]
    for marker in hard_markers:
        if marker in text:
            return "defer"

    easy_markers = [
        "what is", "what are", "define", "definition", "stands for",
        "abbreviation", "simple loop", "repeat", "standard fact",
        "means", "refers to", "stands for", "acronym"
    ]
    if (
        len(question) < 140
        and any(marker in text for marker in easy_markers)
        and ("?" in question or "." not in question.strip())
    ):
        return "nano"

    # Also allow trivial code output tracing (e.g., "What is the output of ...") with a simple check
    if (
        len(question) < 120
        and "output" in question
        and ("for" in question or "loop" in question or "print" in question)
        and not any(marker in text for marker in hard_markers)
    ):
        return "nano"

    return "defer"
# EVOLVE-BLOCK-END

def get_router_prompt():
    return ROUTER_PROMPT
